transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-04
Time: 10:00 AM PT — 10:52 AM PT
Location: Zoom / All-Hands Townhall
Attendees: Priya Rao, Marco Alvarez, Janelle Wu, Samir Patel, Talia Green + All Staff

[00:00] Priya Rao: ok good morning everyone thanks for being on time um we're gonna kick off the Bridgeboard ops and trust roundup, quick agenda: incident debrief, trust & compliance status, perf hotspots and hiring updates. We'll keep this to about 50 minutes and leave time for q and a.

[00:22] Priya Rao: hi uh before I jump in, shout out to the MLOps crew for the weekend rollout, I saw the notes, uh small interruptions but overall smooth. Marco do you want to open on the perf side?

[00:36] Marco Alvarez: yeah thanks Priya, hey folks. So quick context, last week we saw two latency spikes on Dedicated region-us-west-2, uh caused by a combination of a bad kernel selection fallback and some aggressive autoscale churn. We rolled forward a hotfix and patched the kernel selector — that solved the immediate issue. There's still a regression for long sequence workloads when quantization boundaries cross, so Samir and the infra team are doing a deeper bench.

[01:05] Samir Patel: yeah, to add — the KV cache pressure caused some GC-ish pauses, not real GC but memory reclamation interplay with the allocator. We mitigated with a tighter cache eviction policy and reduced the max batch size for that pool. Early numbers show tail latency down ~37% on p95 but there are still p99 pockets on 16k sequences. We're scheduling a dedicated benchmark run.

[01:28] Janelle Wu: can I pause — sorry, this is Janelle — are those p99 pockets affecting hosted API customers or only Dedicated pools?

[01:35] Marco Alvarez: primarily Dedicated; hosted gets a different routing policy and fallbacks so most hosted traffic wasn't elevated. But there was one case where fallback to a variant model increased token cost, which finance flagged.

[01:45] Priya Rao: ok good, thanks. Talia, over to trust — status update on SOC2 and audit readiness?

[01:52] Talia Green: thanks. Short version: SOC2 readiness moved forward but we still have high-priority gaps around logging retention, vendor attestations, and SSO role separation. We're documenting compensating controls where necessary. I've attached the remediation spreadsheet to the notes. We're aiming to close the critical and high items in the next two sprints, timeline goal 2025-09-18 for the public-facing remediation summary.

[02:20] Speaker 1: (murmur) cool.

[02:25] Talia Green: there was a question earlier about KMS integrations — yes, our private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and HSM in VPCs, we still need to finish end-to-end key rotation tests for the on-prem package.

[02:45] Priya Rao: okay great. I want to call out the incident post-mortem process — we did the two-path review, root cause plus systemic risk. We need more instrumentation in the kernel selector to detect divergence earlier. Marco?

[02:58] Marco Alvarez: yes, adding metrics at the kernel opcode level and sampling traces for long-seq flows. We'll feed those into the console traces dashboard and set an alert that triggers when fallback rate exceeds 0.7% over a five-minute window.

[03:20] Priya Rao: cool. On the product side, Janelle?

[03:25] Janelle Wu: thanks. Quick update: the rollout for structured output and function-calling has been delayed two weeks to give eng time to bake in the canary fallback policy and improve contract tests. We're also adding a per-route cost estimate in the console so customers can preview token unit impacts when toggling quantization or batching.

[03:48] Member: (inaudible) will that be in the next console deploy?

[03:51] Janelle Wu: yes, planned for the 09-16 deploy, but dependent on kernel selector metrics being available.

[03:58] Priya Rao: hiring and org — People Ops sent the Q4 headcount ask, linked in the notes. We prioritized infra, trust, and customer success. People Ops will publish hiring cadence by next week. Any questions?

[04:15] Speaker 2: question for Finance: what's the bandwidth for reserved capacity discounts if a customer asks for a multi-region commit?

[04:24] Priya Rao: finance is going to handle case by case, but we want to standardize discount bands. We'll share a draft pricing guardrail with revenue ops by 2025-09-11.

[04:36] Marco Alvarez: one more technical note — NVIDIA driver mismatch across a subset of dedicated nodes caused a subtle mismatch in FP16 kernel scheduling. We quarantined the nodes, and driver roll forward fixed it. We'll add a pre-deploy driver sweep to CI for dedicated images.

[04:58] Talia Green: on compliance, two customers asked for audit logs retention beyond default 90 days for private deployments. We can support via an add-on storage tier but need to bake auditability into the billing events to make it auditable. Action item logged.

[05:15] Audience Member: (someone off mic) is there a plan to advertise these improvements to large customers?

[05:22] Priya Rao: yes, CSM will coordinate a trust notice and targeted outreach to high-commitment accounts. Talia will draft the notice.

[05:30] Priya Rao: ok let's shift to Q and A, please drop questions in chat, will call on folks.

[05:40] [08:15] Anonymous: (chat) Will the SOC2 timeline affect customer POCs?

[05:50] Talia Green: it shouldn't block POCs; we'll offer compensating controls and scoped attestations for POC customers and surface that through solutions engineering.

[06:05] [12:00] Speaker 3: Samir, for the bench runs — can you confirm whether we'll use quantized-only model variants or include mixed precision runs?

[06:12] Samir Patel: we'll do tiered runs: quantized-only, mixed precision, and float32 baseline. That helps isolate kernel vs quantization impact. Expect results by 09-30.

[06:28] [15:00] Speaker 4: Are we deferring any roadmap items because of SOC2 work?

[06:35] Janelle Wu: yes a couple of minor features are deprioritized — advanced usage analytics and a small embedding cache feature. We'll communicate slippage in the product tracker.

[06:48] [19:10] Participant: (soft laugh) hiring — any update on intern programs?

[06:54] Priya Rao: yes summer interns were great, and we'll run another program next year; People Ops to share timeline.

[07:05] [22:45] Marco Alvarez: quick engineering shout, I want to remind teams to follow the feature flag hygiene docs — we had a flag left open that increased fallback surface. Let's be stricter about deletions post-canary.

[07:30] [26:00] Talia Green: tiny privacy note — remember to avoid using customer PII in internal Slack threads for demos; scrub data in shared decks. We've seen a slip in a shared deck that triggered an extra review.

[07:45] [30:00] Priya Rao: ok last section: risk & tradeoffs. We discussed latency vs cost and decided to keep two levers: default hosted conservative kernel selection for safety, and an opt-in permissive profile for customers that want low cost and accept higher variability. We'll document that in the perf guidelines.

[08:10] Audience Member: quick ask— competitor monitoring, are we tracking Anthropic / OpenAI new infra announcements?

[08:18] Marco Alvarez: yes we ingest industry telemetry weekly; but our differentiation is in ops tooling and the unified runtime. We'll add a short weekly note to the leadership digest.

[08:40] Priya Rao: back to actions — recap: Talia publishes SOC2 timeline, Samir runs bench and posts results, Marco shares kernel heatmap, Janelle updates rollout docs, People Ops publishes hiring cadence. Any final questions?

[08:58] [40:00] Speaker 5: (applause) thanks team.

[09:05] Priya Rao: thanks everyone for the focused work. We'll follow up asynchronously and track the action items in the Bridgeboard board. Meeting adjourned.

Notes and attachments: SOC2 remediation spreadsheet (link shared in chat), Kernel selector patch PR #4382 (link), Dedicated benchmark spreadsheet (link).

End of transcript.
